messages:
Alex Chen: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — we still need a concrete plan for charge-assignment when provenance pointers are rewritten during compaction. Do we make assignments immutable (append-only) or support reassignment with a reconciliation pass?
Priya Nair: I'm leaning append-only for the ledger, but we need a deterministic mapping layer so charge queries can follow redirects. Otherwise cost queries change under us. :thinking:
Samir Gupta: Append-only keeps accounting simple, but the pain is backfills. If we add indirection (ownership pointers that can be updated), we must define strong invariants around epochs/leases.
Alex Chen: Exactly. Proposal sketch: keep an append-only event stream (charges) + separate pointer table that maps token_fingerprint -> owner_ref + epoch. Lookups consult pointer table; events store the pointer snapshot at emission time for auditability.
Julian Park: Sounds reasonable. How do we handle late-arriving events that reference a prior epoch? Do we accept them and re-run a reconcile that can emit correcting events?
Priya Nair: Yeah, we'd emit compensating events. Key is making compensations idempotent and easy to stitch. For example, every charge event has a provenance_id and charge_id; reconciliation emits a correction event with reference_charge_id.
Samir Gupta: We need a compact representation in the pointer table. I suggest the pointer record schema:
```
{
  "fingerprint": "sha256:...",
  "owner_ref": "tenant:1234",
  "epoch": "2026-03-15T12:00:00Z",
  "seq": "42"  // bump on every reassignment
}
```
Lookup algorithm: read pointer, if epoch > event.epoch then consult event.epoch of pointer history or fall back to append-only charge.
Ops Lead: How expensive is pointer-history lookups at query time? We can't blow up cost for billing UI.
Alex Chen: We can keep a compact change log per fingerprint (small since ownership changes are rare). For high QPS queries we materialize owner_ref at charge-emit time into a denormalized table used by billing queries. Reconciles update that materialized table asynchronously.
Priya Nair: Migration plan: 1) Start with append-only ledger + materialized owner_ref at emit time. 2) Add pointer table + reconciliation logic behind a feature flag. 3) Run reconciliation in canary customers and verify audit diffs.
Julian Park: Edge-case: what if pointer table is unavailable (network partition)? Emit fallback owner_ref=UNKNOWN or route to burst pool? We should prefer graceful degraded reads (mark as pending) over dropping charges.
Samir Gupta: Agree. Emission path: always write charge event to append-only stream first (sync), then best-effort enrich with pointer lookup. If enrich fails, write event with provenance_hint="PENDING_ENRICH". Reconciler fills in later and emits correction events.
InfraBot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled for refactor branch on staging at 2026-03-22T03:00Z :rocket:
Ops Lead: For audits we must ensure that the audit report can reconstruct owner at any historical point. That means keeping either the pointer history or embedding the owner snapshot in charge events. I prefer embedding owner_snapshot in charge events for 1:1 reconstruction even if redundant.
Alex Chen: Good call. We'll embed owner_snapshot (small fields) in the event envelope to satisfy audit requirements. Reconciler will still emit corrections but auditors can verify original snapshot vs reconciled state.
Priya Nair: Can we add a lightweight checksum to event envelopes so reconciliations can quickly detect divergence? e.g., owner_checksum = sha256(owner_ref + seq)
Samir Gupta: Yup. Also we should add origin_tag = {emitter: service, soft_flag: boolean} so we can identify best-effort enrichments vs authoritative emits.
Julian Park: Sounds like we have the pieces. Next actions: Alex to draft PR with event envelope + pointer table schema, Priya to write reconciliation spec, Samir to prototype canary reconciler, Ops to define audit report acceptance criteria.
Alex Chen: I'll start the PR today and link the small example schema. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
